Header:
Date: 2026-05-22
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Luca Chen (Redwood SE), Oliver Grant (CTO - Synthego), Ayesha Khan (ML Eng), Tom Reyes (Platform)
Meeting recorded via Fireflies

Summary:
Maya and Luca ran a migration/demo walkthrough focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together APIs to Redwood's unified API and Console. Covered API param mapping, streaming, function-calling equivalents, batching/kv-cache optimizations, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, and security (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Customer asked about latency/cost tradeoffs and how Redwood handles model fallbacks and quantized variants. Agreed to run a short benchmark using Synthego's prompt set and share parity doc + pricing.

Topics:
- API parity mapping (models, params, tokens)
- Console demo (routes, keys, cost/latency dashboards)
- Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization)
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC)
- Security & compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
- Next steps and benchmarks

Action items (recap): see metadata

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, welcome, thanks for taking time. I'm Maya, account exec at Redwood, and with me is Luca, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Oliver Grant: Good, thanks. We got a couple hours of orientation but this is fine. I'm ollie, sorry Oliver - CTO at Synthego.
[00:12] Ayesha Khan: Hi, Ayesha here. been looking forward to seeing the parity mapping.
[00:16] Luca Chen: Awesome. Quick agenda - we'll do a short context check, then show the API parity mapping for OpenAI/Anthropic/Together, live console walkthrough, then some Optimize recommendations and Q&A. Sound good?
[00:27] Tom Reyes: Yep, great.
[00:29] Maya Patel: Cool. Oliver, before we jump in, what's your main migration driver? Cost, latency, lock-in?
[00:35] Oliver Grant: All of the above, honestly. We've been on OpenAI for gen and Anthropic for safety-first models, and Together for fine-tuned models. We're seeing rising costs and want more control on latency and on-prem options for regulated parts of our workflow. Also need the ability to run a dedicated pool for high throughput inference.
[00:51] Luca Chen: Makes sense. Are there specific SLAs or P95 latency targets you need?
[00:55] Ayesha Khan: For our main chat product, p95 needs to be under 450ms for 256-token requests. For batch summarization jobs, latency is less critical but throughput matters.
[01:05] Maya Patel: Great, that's helpful. We'll try to map that into the demo. I'll hand off to Luca to show the parity doc and API examples.
[01:12] Luca Chen: Cool. Opening the parity mapping slide, this maps OpenAI/Anthropic/Together params to Redwood API equivalents. For example, openai's model parameter -> model in Redwood, temperature, top_p map directly, but we also expose explicit quantization_profile and routing_policy fields. Function-calling we map to Redwood's structured output + tool-calling shim; the SDK supports the same pattern. Note: sometimes transcription spells 'func-calling' as function calling, right.
[01:42] Oliver Grant: Where do requests route when a model is unavailable? Together had a fallback to their smaller variant.
[01:47] Luca Chen: We have smart routing - you can set routing_policy on a route to prefer latency or cost, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants in the catalog. For Dedicated customers you can pin a variant to avoid fallback.
[01:58] Ayesha Khan: What about streaming? We use streaming a lot for our chat UI.
[02:02] Luca Chen: Streaming is supported; SDK exposes a stream iterator and the Console shows live token metrics. Some minor differences vs OpenAI in chunk framing, but client libs hide that.
[02:12] Maya Patel: I'm going to share my screen and open the Console. (screen share) Alright, this is the Console route list - you can create a route, pick model, set routing policy, and enable kv-cache and prefix caching.
[02:26] [02:26] Tom Reyes: Is the kv cache automatic? We do prefix-heavy traffic.
[02:30] Luca Chen: There's an auto-caching heuristic plus explicit cache TTLs. For chat you can enable prefix caching per route which reduces repeated tokens costs.
[02:38] [02:38] Ayesha Khan: Do you support hardware-aware quantization? We've been experimenting with int4 for some fine-tuned workloads.
[02:44] Luca Chen: Yes, Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles based on workload characteristics. We pick kernels that are quantization-friendly and recommend int8/int4 depending on quality checks. We show expected quality delta and unit-cost savings in the Optimize tab.
[02:57] Maya Patel: Switching to the API tab - here's an example of the parity snippet: OpenAI call with model:"gpt-4x" translates to a Redwood call model:"gpt4x-redwood" or a curated equivalent. We also show parameter mapping and sample responses.
[03:12] [03:12] Luca Chen: I'll paste a live curl example in the chat - here's an OpenAI-style curl and the Redwood equivalent. Note that function-calls become tool definitions in our SDK, and structured output can be validated with a schema.
[03:23] [03:23] Oliver Grant: Any changes required in prompt format or tokenization? We saw token count differences between OpenAI and Anthropic in practice.
[03:30] Luca Chen: Tokenization is model-dependent; we provide tokenizers for the Redwood catalog models. In practice token counts are close but we recommend running a small tokenization comparison during the benchmark. We'll include a tokenization check in the benchmark script.
[03:44] [03:44] Ayesha Khan: On the billing side - how granular are cost reports? We need per-route breakdowns and per-token cost for auditing.
[03:52] Maya Patel: Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route and per-model dashboards. You can export CSVs for billing reconciliation. For Dedicated we also surface billed vs metered usage per reserved pool.
[04:05] [04:05] Tom Reyes: When you say Dedicated, do you support bringing your own infra or is it all Redwood-managed?
[04:10] Luca Chen: Dedicated is Redwood-managed GPU pools in a dedicated tenancy, but for Private we offer a customer-managed control plane and on-prem packaging for air-gapped environments. You can also run the inference runtime in your VPC via our private deployment options.
[04:23] [04:23] Oliver Grant: Security - we need KMS integration, audit logs, SSO and fine-grained RBAC.
[04:28] Maya Patel: We integrate with common KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSMs), provide audit logs, and SSO via SAML. RBAC is supported with roles and token scoping. I'll attach the SOC 2 and network diagram docs after.
[04:40] [04:40] Ayesha Khan: Great. Can we talk about benchmark specifics - sample size, prompt mix, and metrics?
[04:45] Luca Chen: For latency we run p50/p95/p99 on 256-token and 1024-token distributions; for throughput we run sustained qps tests with concurrency settings that mimic your production traffic. We'll also capture quality metrics - perplexity or task-specific accuracy where applicable. We recommend a 2-3 hour run on a small dedicated pool for initial checks.
[05:02] [05:02] Oliver Grant: Sounds good. For quality we mainly care about hallucination rates and instruction-following across our safety prompts.
[05:07] Luca Chen: We'll include your safety prompts in the evaluation set; Redwood's eval harness supports scenario-based tests and regression alerts.
[05:14] [05:14] Tom Reyes: Walk me through the migration steps - we have hundreds of endpoints across microservices, some baked into serverless lambdas.
[05:21] Maya Patel: Common pattern is to start with a single route that mirrors your OpenAI config, point a subset of traffic to Redwood (canary), run benchmarks, then expand. We provide header/route-based routing so you can do gradual rollout. For serverless, the SDK has minimal footprint; we also provide an HTTP adapter that matches OpenAI's semantics to reduce code changes.
[05:40] [05:40] Oliver Grant: Do you have an import tool for existing prompts and models or is it manual?
[05:45] Luca Chen: We have scripts that convert common OpenAI request logs to Redwood route configs and suggestions for model mapping. Fine-tunes and some Together artifacts may need manual migration; we can help with that during the POC.
[05:56] [05:56] Ayesha Khan: Any gotchas with function-calling differences? We rely heavily on function outputs and post-processing hooks.
[06:03] Luca Chen: The behavior is similar; Redwood provides structured output and can call external tools via the tool-calling shim. One difference is the naming of arguments and the model's bias toward output formatting - we'll include examples and a test harness in the benchmark repo.
[06:19] [06:19] Maya Patel: Ok, quick pause - questions so far?
[06:22] [06:22] Oliver Grant: When we talk about model variants, are these all open models or do you carrier proprietary weights too?
[06:29] Luca Chen: Redwood's catalog has a mix - curated open models and partnered variants; we also provide compatibility wrappers to emulate certain API behaviors. For customers needing proprietary weights we support private model hosting under Private deployments.
[06:41] [06:41] Ayesha Khan: How do you guarantee data isolation for regulated pipelines?
[06:45] Maya Patel: For regulated workloads, Private with customer-managed control plane + on-prem runtime provides total isolation. Dedicated gives tenant isolation in Redwood-managed infra and has contractual controls. Both options include KMS and audit logs.
[06:57] [06:57] Tom Reyes: Can we see an example of the Optimize tab and how suggestions look?
[07:00] [07:00] Luca Chen: Switching back to Console - Optimize shows suggestions: batch size recommendations, cache TTLs, suggested quantization profile, and expected cost delta. For example, for your batch summarization workload it suggests batching 8-16 depending on token distribution and a quantization profile int8 with expected ~30% cost reduction and <1% quality delta.
[07:22] [07:22] Ayesha Khan: That's impressive. Do you support automated A/B rollouts if we want to compare quality between models?
[07:28] Luca Chen: Yes, rollouts support canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can tie rollout criteria to latency and quality metrics; if performance regresses, traffic is sent back to the stable model.
[07:40] [07:40] Oliver Grant: For the benchmark, what data do you need from us?
[07:44] Maya Patel: We'll need a prompt set, sample response expectations (if you have labels), a traffic profile (token distribution, concurrency), and any safety test cases.
[07:53] [07:53] Tom Reyes: We'll provide that. Also curious about operational costs for Dedicated - do you charge per GPU hourly plus usage?
[07:59] Luca Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity pricing with monthly commits; on top of that, we surface unit costs per token for burst usage. We'll send a pricing sheet that shows commit tiers, instance types, and expected effective per-token costs at different utilization levels.
[08:13] [08:13] Ayesha Khan: Any examples of customers who moved from OpenAI/Anthropic to Redwood and saw cost reduction?
[08:18] Maya Patel: We have case studies - I'll share a redacted cost-savings example where a customer cut unit cost ~40% after enabling batching and quantization and moving steady-state traffic to Dedicated. I'll attach that doc.
[08:29] [08:29] Oliver Grant: Can we talk briefly about latency overhead for the Console/Control plane vs direct model endpoints?
[08:34] Luca Chen: The control plane only handles routing and metadata; inference path is direct to the runtime. For hosted customers latency difference is minimal - typically a few ms - and for Dedicated the runtime is colocated to minimize hops.
[08:47] [08:47] Maya Patel: Quick live demo - I'll run a Redwood API request that mirrors an OpenAI chat call. (typing/noise)
[08:55] [08:55] Maya Patel: Sending sample - and responses are streaming in, you'll see tokens update.
[09:02] [09:02] Ayesha Khan: I see the stream. Looks similar to what we get now.
[09:06] [09:06] Oliver Grant: Any monitoring hooks? We want traces in our observability stack.
[09:10] Luca Chen: We provide tracing hooks and integrations - you can emit traces to Datadog/NewRelic or export spans via OTLP. Console also has per-request traces and token-level timing breakdowns.
[09:23] [09:23] Tom Reyes: For PII retention rules, can we set retention on a per-route basis?
[09:27] Maya Patel: Yes, retention is configurable per-route and per-tenant; retention policies tie into audit logs and can be enforced by policy.
[09:34] [09:34] Ayesha Khan: Ok here's a specific question - our Together models use a custom fine-tune with a slightly different tokenization. Will Redwood host that fine-tune or do we re-run training?
[09:43] Luca Chen: For Together fine-tunes you'll typically bring the model artifacts; Redwood can host the fine-tuned artifact in Private or Dedicated depending on licensing. If needed we help re-quantize and validate quality.
[09:55] [09:55] Oliver Grant: Can you share the parity mapping now?
[09:58] Maya Patel: Pasting link to parity doc in chat - (link) It lists param mappings, model equivalents, and example curl/SDK snippets.
[10:06] [10:06] Ayesha Khan: Thanks. We'll review.
[10:09] [10:09] Luca Chen: Quick note on rate limits - Redwood supports burst capacity and quota configs per route; the Console can throttle or queue. That helps with serverless cold starts.
[10:21] [10:21] Tom Reyes: Do you have example terraform/cloudformation to provision network connectivity for Private?
[10:26] Maya Patel: Yes, we have terraform modules and network diagrams. We'll share the repo link in the follow-up.
[10:34] [10:34] Oliver Grant: Ok, last set of questions - what's typical POC duration and success criteria?
[10:38] Luca Chen: Typical POC is 2-6 weeks: week 1 onboarding and small benchmark, weeks 2-3 deeper evals and configs, final week rollout plan and TCO. Success criteria we usually define as: parity in quality (within X% on labeled tests), p95 latency under agreed SLO, and target cost reductions or throughput targets. We'll write these into the POC charter.
[10:58] [10:58] Ayesha Khan: That timeline works. We'll try to get sample prompts to you by Monday.
[11:02] [11:02] Maya Patel: Fantastic. To recap - we'll send parity mapping + pricing, SOC2/security docs, and Luca will prep benchmark scripts. Customer to send sample prompts and traffic profile.
[11:11] [11:11] Oliver Grant: Perfect. Thanks both.
[11:13] [11:13] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with calendar invite for the benchmark kick-off.
[11:18] [11:18] Call ended.
